methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Virginia's AI challenge isn't data centers. It's small-business adoption | Guest column - richmond.com
signals.signal_reading: Guest column explicitly frames Virginia's AI challenge as small-business adoption failure, signaling that infrastructure focus (data centers) may be masking shallow penetration into actual economic activity across the commonwealth's diverse business base.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - news.vcu.edu
signals.signal_reading: VCU partnership with AI Ready RVA creates institutional infrastructure for distributed education and community impact, potentially building peer-to-peer learning networks that spread deep capability beyond elite tech hubs.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Workforce pressure on Richmond's young talent signals metro concentration of AI demand, creating capability clustering in capital region while potentially draining skills from surrounding areas without equivalent opportunity structures.

signals.title: University of Virginia Students Help Businesses Explore AI - GovTech
signals.signal_reading: UVA students helping businesses explore AI represents peer-distributed knowledge transfer model that could spread deep understanding beyond consultancy-driven adoption, though reach beyond university-connected businesses remains uncertain.

signals.title: ‘Shaping our future’: Company powering AI data centers invests $50+ million in Henrico, adding 200 jobs - WWBT
signals.signal_reading: 50M investment adding 200 AI infrastructure jobs in Henrico reinforces metro concentration pattern—capital flows to data center supply chains in established hubs rather than distributing AI application capability to underserved regions.
